paragraphs.source_en: Yet at this moment, Ieyasu once again received Date Masamune, who had come to bid him farewell—a most unusual thing. Even Lord Hideyoshi, who had never concealed his illness, kept his closest retainers in the dark as death approached; Ieyasu alone declared that he wished to see Masamune.

paragraphs.source_en: No matter how heroic a man may be, his mind will often become confused when death confronts him; yet Ieyasu was exceedingly lucid now. Yagyū Munenori sat to one side, seemingly forgotten by everyone. Perhaps for that very reason, he was able to observe every face in silence. He judged that Ieyasu would not pass away within the next few days; at the same time, he understood why the loyal Katayama Sōtetsu had been banished.

paragraphs.source_en: Since Sōtetsu’s banishment, Ieyasu had scarcely allowed physicians near him. units.source_zh: 敕使去后，四月初一到初五，众人日日守护于榻旁，生怕有急。

units.source_en: The whole of Sunpu was shrouded in tension.
units.source_zh: 整座骏府笼罩在紧张之中。

paragraphs.source_zh: 敕使去后，四月初一到初五，众人日日守护于榻旁，生怕有急。整座骏府笼罩在紧张之中。

paragraphs.source_en: On the sixth day of the fourth month, Ieyasu improved a little once more.

units.source_en: On the sixth day of the fourth month, Ieyasu improved a little once more.
units.source_zh: 四月初六，家康又有了一些好转。

paragraphs.source_zh: 四月初六，家康又有了一些好转。

paragraphs.source_en: Until then he had taken almost neither food nor water, but that day he managed to drink some thin gruel. Though it was only a small cup each time, after drinking it two or three times he gradually became lucid.

units.source_en: Until then he had taken almost neither food nor water, but that day he managed to drink some thin gruel. Though it was only a small cup each time, after drinking it two or three times he gradually became lucid.
units.source_zh: 在此之前，他几已水米不进，但此日他竟喝了些稀粥，每次虽皆只一小杯，但喝过两三次，人逐渐清醒了。

paragraphs.source_zh: 在此之前，他几已水米不进，但此日他竟喝了些稀粥，每次虽皆只一小杯，但喝过两三次，人逐渐清醒了。

paragraphs.source_en: His close retainers began cautiously asking him questions.

units.source_en: His close retainers began cautiously asking him questions.

ja.t: しにいくつかのことを

units.source_zh: 亲信开始试着问他一些话。

paragraphs.source_zh: 亲信开始试着问他一些话。

paragraphs.source_en: On the morning of the sixth, Hidetada, his worried brow somewhat eased, came before Ieyasu with the three elders Zonnō, Ryōteki, and Kakuzan of Zōjōji in Edo, and Elder Rodō of Daijuji in Mikawa.

units.source_en: On the morning of the sixth, Hidetada, his worried brow somewhat eased, came before Ieyasu with the three elders Zonnō, Ryōteki, and Kakuzan of Zōjōji in Edo, and Elder Rodō of Daijuji in Mikawa.
units.source_zh: 初六晨，略展愁眉的秀忠带着江户增上寺的存应、了的、廓山三位长老和三河大树寺的鲁道长老，来到家康跟前。

paragraphs.source_zh: 初六晨，略展愁眉的秀忠带着江户增上寺的存应、了的、廓山三位长老和三河大树寺的鲁道长老，来到家康跟前。

paragraphs.source_en: Bringing monks from Edo and Mikawa before a sick man required immense courage. If Ieyasu was still lucid, he would surely give some instructions concerning his funeral.

units.source_en: Bringing monks from Edo and Mikawa before a sick man required immense courage.
units.source_zh: 把江户和三河的僧人带至病人面前，实需莫大的勇气。

units.source_en: If Ieyasu was still lucid, he would surely give some instructions concerning his funeral.
units.source_zh: 如果家康还清醒，必会对葬礼有些吩咐。

paragraphs.source_zh: 把江户和三河的僧人带至病人面前，实需莫大的勇气。如果家康还清醒，必会对葬礼有些吩咐。

paragraphs.source_en: After reporting that the elders of the two temples had come to visit him in his illness, Hidetada changed the subject. He began consulting his father about granting Mizuno Tadakiyo an additional stipend of ten thousand koku and having Ishikawa Tadafusa inherit Ienari’s house and estate. He wanted to test whether his father was still lucid—whether the name Ishikawa Ienari would lead him to think of Ishikawa Kazumasa’s descendants, and from them to Ōkubo Tadachika.

units.source_en: After reporting that the elders of the two temples had come to visit him in his illness, Hidetada changed the subject.
units.source_zh: 秀忠禀告完两寺的长老们前来探病，便把话题岔开了。

units.source_en: He began consulting his father about granting Mizuno Tadakiyo an additional stipend of ten thousand koku and having Ishikawa Tadafusa inherit Ienari’s house and estate.
units.source_zh: 他开始与父亲商量为水野忠清加封一万石俸禄，及令石川忠总继承家成家业诸事。

units.source_en: He wanted to test whether his father was still lucid—whether the name Ishikawa Ienari would lead him to think of Ishikawa Kazumasa’s descendants, and from them to Ōkubo Tadachika.

units.source_zh: 他是想试探父亲是否还清醒，想试试父亲能否从石川家成想到石川数正的子孙，再想到大久保忠邻。

paragraphs.source_zh: 秀忠禀告完两寺的长老们前来探病，便把话题岔开了。他开始与父亲商量为水野忠清加封一万石俸禄，及令石川忠总继承家成家业诸事。他是想试探父亲是否还清醒，想试试父亲能否从石川家成想到石川数正的子孙，再想到大久保忠邻。

paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu agreed to all of Hidetada’s proposals. “It is very good that Ienari’s house should be restored. When the opportunity arises, do something for Ōkubo as well... I leave it to you.” He had brought up Ōkubo Tadachika of his own accord.

units.source_en: Ieyasu agreed to all of Hidetada’s proposals.
units.source_zh: 家康同意秀忠诸议。

units.source_en: “It is very good that Ienari’s house should be restored.

units.source_zh: “为家成恢复家业，如此甚好。

units.source_en: When the opportunity arises, do something for Ōkubo as well... I leave it to you.”
units.source_zh: 找个机会，给大久保也……就交与你了。”

units.source_en: He had brought up Ōkubo Tadachika of his own accord.
units.source_zh: 他竟主动提起了大久保忠邻。

paragraphs.source_zh: 家康同意秀忠诸议。“为家成恢复家业，如此甚好。找个机会，给大久保也……就交与你了。”他竟主动提起了大久保忠邻。

paragraphs.source_en: Just then, learning that Ieyasu was still lucid, Tōdō Takatora suddenly entered from the adjoining room. “My lord, I beg you to accept me as your disciple.”

units.source_en: Just then, learning that Ieyasu was still lucid, Tōdō Takatora suddenly entered from the adjoining room. “My lord, I beg you to accept me as your disciple.”
units.source_zh: 正在这时，藤堂高虎得知家康尚清醒，忽从隔室进来，“大人，请大人收在下为弟子。”

paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu opened his eyes and looked. Dimly, he saw that Takatora had shaved off his grizzled hair and donned a monk’s robe.

units.source_en: Ieyasu opened his eyes and looked. Dimly, he saw that Takatora had shaved off his grizzled hair and donned a monk’s robe.

paragraphs.source_zh: 家康睁眼一看，隐约见高虎已剃去花白头发，身披袈裟。

paragraphs.source_en: “My lord, you are the greatest man I have encountered in this world. Please accept me as your disciple and let me accompany you on the road to the underworld!”

paragraphs.source_en: It was a plea to follow his lord in death. Ieyasu stared at Takatora in astonishment.

units.source_en: It was a plea to follow his lord in death.
units.source_zh: 此为殉死之求。

units.source_en: Ieyasu stared at Takatora in astonishment.
units.source_zh: 家康惊讶地盯着高虎。

paragraphs.source_en: Because Ieyasu’s words were so startlingly clear, Tōdō Takatora, who had by then lost all composure, raised his head in bewilderment.

units.source_en: Because Ieyasu’s words were so startlingly clear, Tōdō Takatora, who had by then lost all composure, raised his head in bewilderment.
units.source_zh: 由于家康口齿过于清晰，此时已失去心智的藤堂高虎茫然地抬起头来。

paragraphs.source_zh: 由于家康口齿过于清晰，此时已失去心智的藤堂高虎茫然地抬起头来。

paragraphs.source_en: “To follow another in death is to claim one’s life as one’s own... You must not!”

units.source_en: “To follow another in death is to claim one’s life as one’s own... You must not!”
units.source_zh: “所谓殉死，便是要把性命据为己有……不可！”

paragraphs.source_zh: “所谓殉死，便是要把性命据为己有……不可！”

paragraphs.source_en: “Even after I have shaved my head like this, my lord, will you still not accept me as your disciple?”

units.source_en: “Even after I have shaved my head like this, my lord, will you still not accept me as your disciple?”

ja.t: にしてくださらぬのですか」

paragraphs.source_zh: “即便如在下这般剃掉了头发，大人也不愿收在下为弟子？”

paragraphs.source_en: “If you are my disciple...” Ieyasu glanced around at the temple elders by his pillow, drew a breath, and said, “When even my own life does not belong to me, how could I take a disciple’s life at my whim?”

paragraphs.source_en: Takatora began to speak, then stopped. He had often heard Ieyasu say that all things possess a vital center. The vital center of Japan was Ise. But only now did Takatora truly understand: looking back through history, there had never been an age or dynasty in which Ise lay neglected while all the people lived in peace and happiness. The Grand Shrine of Ise was the vital center of peace throughout the realm—indeed, it was peace itself.

paragraphs.source_en: “What did Father say?”

paragraphs.source_en: “I ought to have died on the battlefield, yet now I have been able to entrust each of my wishes to you all. I can depart without regret.”

units.source_en: “I ought to have died on the battlefield, yet now I have been able to entrust each of my wishes to you all. I can depart without regret.”
units.source_zh: “我原本应死于疆场上，现在却能将心愿一一托与众人，毫无遗憾离去了。”

paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu’s reflection sent a ripple through those assembled. He had entrusted his wishes, one by one, to everyone—yet among them there was no place for Tadateru, the Kazusa-no-suke. For Lady Chaa, Tadateru’s mother, who had attended to Ieyasu’s daily needs for many years, this was a heart-rending agony. With a wail, she burst into tears...

paragraphs.source_zh: 家康的感慨掀起了一阵波澜。他把心愿一一托给大家，在这其中，独无上总介忠辉。这对于照料家康起居多年的忠辉生母茶阿局，却是撕心裂肺的痛，她“哇”一声哭了起来……
